why: Found at the M6 landing by the lead (the landing runner). R1 compares the sha256 of each pinned file of the existing frontends at HEAD with its pin, so it judges later keys too. I103 (#172) changes five of them (holon/frontends/go/extract.py and holon/frontends/solidity/__init__.py, ast.py, compile.py and transitions.py: solc by pragma, go by directive, the go.work rule), so R1 fails on the merged tree although I105 changed none. Its contract is that I105 leaves the existing frontends unchanged. The amended check reads each pinned file at I105's landed head d13ab328 (#170's head, merged by the M6 landing) and compares its sha256 with the same pin; all 18 hold there. The pins, the paths and the assertion are unchanged. As HUMAN_ANSWERS Q48 narrowed I48-R3 and I52-B7 to their own keys.

Ruling change (HUMAN_ANSWERS Q64, Q67; delegated by the lead on #179): Q64 made machines.nil_maps "unknown" the Go machine frontend's default (I109 (g)); this test relied on the old default, under which a config without the key carried no nil_map debt. Q67: a test is never left out of its CI job, so it is amended to name the mode it was written for, the explicit opt-out "zero", in a temp copy of its config (the fixture files are not edited). Every assertion is unchanged. On the default path the demo is re-decided UNKNOWN, checked by I109's TestNilMapDefault.test_p6_i105_demo_redecided_unknown; the opt-out path exercises the pipeline, which Q60 marks unsound for decisions.
